GazettePro · Venezuelan tax law · sample corpus

Venezuelan tax law, organized the way you research US tax law

Sources are ranked by authority, from the Constitution and the treaty down to SENIAT rules and Treasury commentary. Every section has a permanent link, a Bluebook-style citation and its status in any year since 1994.

Start from the source index, search across every text, or ask the assistant, whose answers cite the exact article. This sample holds the US–Venezuela income tax treaty and Protocol with the Technical Explanation, the Código Orgánico Tributario of 2020, the IVA law and the Ley Orgánica de Aduanas as republished in 2020, the 2014 text of the Ley de Impuesto sobre la Renta, the Ley Orgánica de Hidrocarburos and its 2026 Reglamento, all in full, plus the SENIAT rules on special taxpayers (SNAT/2026/00099) and invoicing (SNAT/2026/00093) and excerpts of the Constitution.

    Search tips

    • Natural language: type a question or plain words, e.g. withholding on dividends to a US company.
    • Terms & connectors: "permanent establishment" w/s construction, contribuyent! AND domicilio, interest w/5 bank OR financial.
    • Get by citation: COT 91, treaty 10(2)(a), SNAT 3(e), CRBV 317, Protocol 11.

    Reference graph

      How Radar uses it

      A new tax law is published but says nothing about when it takes effect. Radar follows the graph to set the urgency date:

      CRBV art. 317 ¶4 + COT art. 8 ¶1
      → in force 60 continuous days after publication

      Providencia SNAT/2026/00099 is not a law, so the 60-day default does not apply. Its art. 18 sets the date itself: in force 1 November 2026, nine days after publication, which gives Radar the maximum urgency score.

      Fines under COT arts. 91–92 are computed at the BCV highest-value currency rate on the payment date, so the app can show the live amount of any penalty.

      Special-taxpayer check

      Uses the thresholds tagged in arts. 2–3. Enter amounts already converted at the BCV rate for the highest-value currency.

      Example figures. Exclusions in art. 4 (new ventures, primary agriculture, comunas, first year of operations) are not checked here.

      Hydrocarbon fiscal take

      Royalty plus impuesto integrado by project type, from Reglamento LOH art. 43, applied to the value of hydrocarbons extracted and not reinjected (LOH art. 55).

      The specific rates are set project by project (Reglamento art. 44). The Reglamento does not say whether the two reductions can be combined. Income tax: 34% for Greenfield projects (art. 45); other projects pay the Ley de ISLR rate unless reduced under LOH art. 58.

      Status signals

      In force Current text, no negative history in this corpus.
      Caution In force, but amended recently or its validity is questioned.
      Repealed No longer in force; shown for history.
      Not yet effective Published, with a later effective date.
      Secondary source Commentary or explanation, not law.

      Signals are computed for today's date from the version history in the source index. Tap a signal on any article to read why.

      Export the source index

      Radar scores each act against three sample business profiles (0–100). Acts that reach none of them score 0 and would be filtered out of a client's feed.

      Statute timeline

      Which version of each source applies on a given date. Drag the line across the chart or type a date; the list below shows what governs that day, what has been published but is not yet in force, and the gazettes and decisions up to then.

      Topical index

      Subjects A to Z across every source, in the style of a code index. Spanish terms are given in italics and cross-referenced. Citations use subsection form: art. 10(2)(a) means article 10, paragraph 2, subparagraph a.

    Unofficial reading copy for demonstration. The legal originals are the PDFs of Gaceta Oficial N° 6.507 Extraordinario (29 Jan 2020) for the COT, and N° 5.453 Extraordinario (24 Mar 2000) with Enmienda N° 1 in N° 5.908 Extraordinario (19 Feb 2009) for the Constitution.
    The COT, the Ley Orgánica de Aduanas and the IVA law were extracted from the text layer of the same gazette PDF (pp. 2–36, 42–61 and 64–74) and checked word for word against it. The customs and IVA texts are the full texts the gazette republished after each reform; their in-force dates (19 Feb and 29 Mar 2020) are computed from their final articles. Verify every text against the official gazette before relying on it.
    US–Venezuela Convention and Protocol (signed Caracas, 25 Jan 1999; effective 1 Jan 2000) and the US Treasury Technical Explanation, generated from the US government texts. The Spanish text of the treaty is equally authentic and is not included yet.
    Providencia SNAT/2026/00093 (invoicing) extracted from the text layer of Gaceta Oficial N° 43.484, pp. 473.381–473.388, and checked word for word; its effective date (19 Apr 2027) is computed from the 180-day rule in Disposición Final Octava.
    Providencia SNAT/2026/00099 transcribed from the image PDF of Gaceta Oficial N° 43.485, pp. 473.398–473.399, keeping the original spelling.
    Ley Orgánica de Hidrocarburos: consolidated text (texto único) published with the reform in Gaceta Oficial N° 6.978 Extraordinario (29 Jan 2026). Reglamento: Decreto N° 5.381, Gaceta Oficial N° 7.052 Extraordinario (7 July 2026). Both extracted from the gazette PDFs; the effective date of the fiscal articles (31 Mar 2026) is computed from the 60-day rule in the Law.
    Ley de Impuesto sobre la Renta: texto único published with Decreto N° 1.435 in Gaceta Oficial N° 6.152 Extraordinario (18 Nov 2014), read by OCR from the scanned gazette and corrected by dictionary and rules; the rate tables were typed from the page image. Small OCR errors may remain. The December 2015 reform (G.O. N° 6.210 Ext.) is not in this sample.
